name: confirmedLicensePurchased
definition: The vendor reports an active entitlement (licence or subscription) for the product the integration connects to. Licence evidence, not control evidence: a true says the customer owns the tool, nothing about whether it is configured or working.
population: the connected vendor account or tenant
evidenceRequiredForTrue: A vendor response that states the account's licence or subscription is active. A successful authenticated call alone is not that evidence; a field synthesised by our own connector's returnSpec is evidence only of what the returnSpec reads.

aliases.name: hasValidLicense
aliases.note: Qualys RTA row whose file returns only confirmedLicensePurchased; plan B2b deletes the row as a pure alias. Registered here so the spelling cannot be minted again with a different meaning.

conflict.summary: The meaning is broadly agreed (entitlement) across 92 integrations, 70 files and 126 requirements. The TYPE is not: one implementation returns the strings "confirmed"/"unconfirmed" and states its requirement compares isEquals "confirmed", while the requirements surface declares isEquals with a boolean value. Only the type is contested, so new integrations may still answer the key (integrationPolicy any).

positions.meaning: Boolean: the vendor reports an active licence.

positions.source: Read for this entry. Its no-evidence branches return "unconfirmed", a measured-looking answer, not null. No requirement in the 2026-10-06 requirements snapshot compares this key to the string "confirmed"; whether Token-Service's fuzzyEquals matches "confirmed" against a boolean true is unverified, so this verified integration's licence check may be unsatisfiable today.

proposedResolution.summary: Boolean, with null when not measured. Keepit moves to a boolean; the 2026-10-06 requirements snapshot holds no requirement comparing to "confirmed", so the switch should strand nothing -- confirm against live requirements before shipping.

decision.question: Confirm confirmedLicensePurchased is boolean everywhere, and whether licence evidence should ever satisfy a control requirement or only a separate entitlement check -- it is asked under 16 category spellings today, so Wave F moves it more than any other key.

notes: Plan F staging calls 1b 'one boolean: the cheapest possible V3'. Category-unlocking 1b integrations does not require the key to be V3; it requires each unmasked implementation to be.
